hints.title: Element Order Independence
hints.text: The width of a subsequence depends only on its minimum and maximum elements, not their original relative positions.

hints.title: Sorted Array Position Multipliers
hints.text: Sort the array. An element at index i acts as the maximum in 2 raised to i subsequences and as the minimum in 2 raised to (n - 1 - i) subsequences.

hints.title: Linear Combinatorial Contribution
hints.text: Multiply each sorted element by (2^i - 2^(n - 1 - i)) modulo 10^9 + 7 and sum across all indices.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def sumSubseqWidths(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        nums.sort()
        n = len(nums)
        pow2 = [1] * n
        for i in range(1, n):
            pow2[i] = (pow2[i - 1] * 2) % MOD

        ans = 0
        for i in range(n):
            ans = (ans + nums[i] * (pow2[i] - pow2[n - 1 - i])) % MOD
        return (ans + MOD) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Sorting followed by linear pass with precomputed powers of two.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N subsequences takes exponential time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Notice order independence, sort the array, and count maximum versus minimum appearances.
